slot.brief: find the equation of tangent and normal to an implicitly defined curve (e.g. x²+xy+y² = c) at a given point via implicit differentiation

stem: The equation of the tangent to the curve $x^2 + xy + y^2 = 13$ at the point $(1,3)$ is

verdicts.working: At (1,3), the gradient of x² + xy + y² is (5,7). Thus the tangent is 5(x−1) + 7(y−3) = 0, or 5x + 7y = 26.

working:
Implicit differentiation: $2x + y + x\frac{dy}{dx} + 2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{2x+y}{x+2y}$. At $(1,3)$, slope $m = -\frac{5}{7}$. Tangent: $y-3 = -\frac{5}{7}(x-1) \Rightarrow 5x+7y=26$.

Independent check: At (1,3), the gradient of x² + xy + y² is (5,7). Thus the tangent is 5(x−1) + 7(y−3) = 0, or 5x + 7y = 26.
solution:
Implicit differentiation gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{2x+y}{x+2y}$, so at $(1,3)$ the slope is $-\dfrac57$. Hence
$$y-3=-\frac57(x-1)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 5x+7y=26.$$
